key_insight: This paper shows how to adapt a pretrained object-centric 3D generator so it can build complete scenes from just one image, instead of being limited to isolated objects or indoor-only settings. The key breakthrough is redesigning the generator to handle both indoor and outdoor scenes while filling in unseen geometry.
problem_solved: Single-image scene generation is hard because the model must infer unseen parts of a 3D scene from limited visual evidence. Existing pretrained 3D generators are typically object-focused, assume a fixed canonical volume, and do not transfer well to diverse outdoor environments.
method: Redesign a pretrained object-centric 3D generator (e.g., Trellis 2) for scene-level generation.
Adapt the representation and generation pipeline so it can support both indoor and outdoor scenes.
Leverage the strong prior learned from 3D object data to hallucinate occluded or unobserved surfaces from a single input image.
impact: This work makes single-image 3D reconstruction more practical for real-world scenes, not just isolated objects. For practitioners, it suggests a path to reuse strong pretrained 3D object models for broader scene understanding and generation tasks.
